{{Short description|Theorem in algebraic geometry}}
{{distinguish|Le Potier's vanishing theorem}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Bogomolov–Sommese vanishing theorem''' is a result related to the [[Kodaira–Itaka dimension]]. It is named after [[Fedor Bogomolov]] and [[Andrew Sommese]]. Its statement has differing versions:

{{blockquote|'''Bogomolov–Sommese vanishing theorem for snc pair''':<ref>{{harv|Michałek|2012}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Greb|Kebekus|Kovács|2010}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Esnault|Viehweg|1992|loc=Corollary 6.9}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Kebekus|2013|loc=Theorem 2.17}}</ref> Let ''X'' be a projective manifold (smooth [[projective variety]]), ''D'' a simple [[normal crossing divisor]] (snc divisor) and <math>A \subseteq \Omega ^{p} _ {X} (\log D)</math> an [[invertible sheaf|invertible subsheaf]]. Then the Kodaira–Itaka dimension <math>\kappa(A)</math> is not greater than ''p''.
}}

This result is equivalent to the statement that:<ref>{{harv|Graf|2015}}</ref>

:<math>H^{0}\left(X,A^{- 1} \otimes \Omega ^{p}_{X} (\log D) \right) = 0</math>

for every complex projective snc pair <math>(X, D)</math> and every [[invertible sheaf#The Picard group|invertible sheaf]] <math>A \in \mathrm{Pic}(X)</math>
with <math>\kappa(A) > p</math>.

Therefore, this theorem is called the vanishing theorem.

{{blockquote|'''Bogomolov–Sommese vanishing theorem for lc pair''':<ref>{{harv|Greb|Kebekus|Kovács|Peternell|2011|loc=Theorem 7.2}}</ref><ref>{{harv|Kebekus|2013|loc=Corollary 4.14 }}</ref> Let (X,D) be a [[log canonical]] pair, where X is projective. If <math>A \subseteq\Omega ^{[p]}_{X} (\log \lfloor D \rfloor)</math> is a <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>-Cartier [[Reflexive sheaf|reflexive subsheaf]] of rank one,<ref>{{harv|Greb|Kebekus|Kovács|Peternell|2011|loc=Definition 2.20.}}</ref> then <math>\kappa(A) \leq p</math>.}}
